key_insight: Visual features are more stable than noisy labels—guiding prompt learning with vision signals makes cross-modal prompts robust to label noise while remaining lightweight.
problem_solved: Prompt-based vision–language models degrade when training labels are noisy because learned prompts overfit incorrect labels; this work makes prompt learning resilient to noisy supervision.
method: Introduce a lightweight vision-guided prompt module that conditions prompt tokens on image features (cross-modal guidance) rather than relying solely on label supervision.
Use a cross-modal alignment mechanism to decouple prompt updates from noisy textual labels, letting reliable visual semantics steer prompt learning.
Design a plug-and-play, parameter-efficient component compatible with existing vision–language backbones (e.g., CLIP-like models) for training under noisy-label regimes.
impact: Enables practitioners to train prompt-tuned vision–language systems reliably on noisy or weakly labeled datasets without expensive label-cleaning, improving robustness in real-world deployment.

paper_title: Seeing is Believing: Robust Vision-Guided Cross-Modal Prompt Learning under Label Noise
paper_authors: Zibin Geng, Xuefeng Jiang, Jia Li, Zheng Li, Tian Wen
